scenarios.desc: Main went red and a retro is needed
scenarios.input: `main` went red yesterday after a merge and I am writing the retro at .project-toolkit/retrospective/main-red.md. What must the file contain? Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: MUST 1 to 4: the filename is YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md, the failure is classified against .agents/governance/FAILURE-MODES.md, evidence links commits, PRs, or CI runs, and remediation lists follow-ups with owners or issues. 'main went red' is one of the four triggers.

scenarios.desc: Request to soften a landed retro
scenarios.input: A landed retro docs/retros/2026-10-02-bad-deploy.md names a teammate's decision harshly. I want to edit the existing sentences to soften it. How do I proceed? Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: MUST NOT 1 forbids deleting or editing landed retros to soften criticism, so corrections append a new dated section with rationale. MUST 5 requires critiquing processes and artifacts, never individuals.

scenarios.desc: Remediation commit for a retro finding
scenarios.input: The retro .project-toolkit/retrospective/2026-11-02-hook-wedge.md lists a governance fix. I am about to commit the fix with the message `fix(rules): tighten hook path rule`. Anything missing? Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: MUST NOT 2: remediation commits must not ship without linking the retro in the commit body or PR.

scenarios.input: I am writing .project-toolkit/retrospective/2026-11-10-stale-mirror.md. Nothing in the failure taxonomy fits the problem. Can I just label it 'other'? Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: MUST 2: if no existing class in .agents/governance/FAILURE-MODES.md matches, the retro MUST propose a new class in a linked ADR.

scenarios.desc: Fixing a typo in an existing failure-mode taxonomy row (negative)
scenarios.input: I want to fix a typo in a row of .agents/governance/FAILURE-MODES.md. Which steps apply? Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: The rule's paths are .project-toolkit/retrospective/** and docs/retros/**. The taxonomy file sits in neither, so the retro file clauses do not apply.

scenarios.desc: Teammate asks for a scheduled retro on a quiet day
scenarios.input: Nothing failed today: no red main, no revert, no user correction, no reflect finding, and no pull request was closed. A teammate says we must still drop a daily file in docs/retros/ to satisfy the pre-push habit. Is a retro owed? Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: When To Write One: retros are event-triggered, never scheduled. None of the four triggers fired, and no pull request closed, so no retrospective trigger fired. (The Post-PR Retrospective workflow was deleted on 2026-11-25.) A day like that owes no retrospective. The removed daily gate is the carve-out, so no retro file is authored.

scenarios.desc: Draft retro blames the person who merged
scenarios.input: Main went red after PR 7412 merged. I am drafting the write-up and want to say that Dana merged without running tests and should be more careful. Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: MUST 5: critique processes and artifacts, never individuals. The write-up names the missing gate, not the person, and links the commit and the CI run (MUST 3).

scenarios.desc: Retro saved under an ad hoc name
scenarios.input: I will save the write-up for last night's revert as retro-main-red.md in .project-toolkit/retrospective/ and describe what happened in a few paragraphs. Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: MUST 1: new retros use YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md. MUST 2 to 4 also require a failure-mode class, evidence links, and remediation actions.

scenarios.desc: Remediation section that says to be more careful
scenarios.input: The remediation section of my write-up on the broken release says the team should be more careful with config changes and double-check before merging. Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: MUST 4: remediation lists concrete follow-up actions (governance change, ADR, instruction update, skill change) with owners or issues. Be more careful is not an action.

scenarios.input: I need a changelog entry that summarizes this week's merged PRs, grouped by feature, fix, and chore, with PR links. Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: A changelog is release communication, not a failure analysis. No retrospective trigger fired and no retro file is involved.
